catalogue: Australian internal wall-lining and ceiling construction

objects.name: internal wall-lining and ceiling system
objects.definition: The coordinated internal wall and ceiling sheets, boards, panels, support members, fixings, joints, trims and finishes that form the visible room-side surfaces of a building.
functions: Cover internal framing or solid substrates
Form finished wall and ceiling planes
Coordinate openings, joints, edges and performance-specific lining layers

ncc_references.relationship: Calls up AS 5637.1 for specified fire-hazard assessment of wall and ceiling linings; the resulting classification is evidence attached to a selected product or system.

cad.pattern: Connected wall and ceiling surface assemblies divided at changes of material, support, layer build-up, joints and openings
cad.placement: Room side of internal and external walls and below or between roof and floor structure
cad.start: Floor, wall or ceiling boundary and substrate
cad.end: Finished visible surface and perimeter trim
cad.opening: Doors, windows, services, access panels and control joints remain explicit
cad.load: Self-weight and incidental service loads transferred through fixings and supports; not assumed structural bracing

notes: A lining is the covering layer or assembly; skirting, cornice, architrave and electrical accessories are attached objects, not automatically part of the lining material.

objects.name: internal wall-lining assembly
objects.definition: A complete room-side wall covering made from one or more lining layers together with its supports where used, fixings, joints, perimeter edges and openings.
functions: Create a continuous internal wall face
Conceal and protect the wall substrate or cavity
Carry the selected decorative and performance finish

cad.pattern: Planar wall-face assembly repeated by room and material zone
cad.placement: On framing, battens, furring or a solid wall substrate
cad.start: Wall base or nominated lower termination
cad.end: Ceiling, soffit or nominated upper termination
cad.opening: Cut around door, window, niche, service and access openings
cad.load: Lining self-weight and attached light-duty items transferred to supports or substrate

notes: Performance labels such as fire, acoustic, impact or wet-area grade require a selected tested or documented system and are not inferred from appearance.

objects.name: plasterboard wall-lining assembly
objects.definition: An internal wall lining built from gypsum plasterboard sheets fixed to framing, battens, furring or an approved solid-substrate system and completed with the specified joints and edges.
functions: Form a smooth internal wall surface
Provide a substrate for decoration
Contribute selected fire, sound, impact or moisture properties when part of a documented system

cad.pattern: Rectangular sheets tiled across a wall face with explicit recessed and butt joints
cad.placement: Room side of a framed, furred or documented direct-fixed wall
cad.end: Last supported sheet edge or movement joint
cad.opening: Sheets are cut and trimmed around openings without assuming unsupported joints
cad.load: Sheet self-weight transferred through fasteners and any adhesive to wall supports

notes: Gyprock is a trade mark used colloquially for plasterboard and is retained only as a search alias.

objects.name: direct-fixed plasterboard masonry lining assembly
objects.definition: A plasterboard lining bonded and locally supported directly against an internal masonry or concrete face using a documented direct-fix system without a separate continuous furring cavity.
functions: Create a smooth face over masonry or concrete
Avoid a full framed lining cavity
Transfer lining weight through compatible adhesive and local supports to the solid substrate

cad.pattern: Sheet field offset from a solid wall by discrete adhesive beds
cad.placement: Internal face of suitable masonry or concrete
cad.opening: Perimeters and openings require supported, sealed or trimmed terminations from the selected system
cad.load: Sheet self-weight transferred through cured adhesive beds and specified support details

notes: The familiar overseas term dot and dab is not treated as the preferred Australian system name or as a universal adhesive pattern.

objects.name: furred masonry wall-lining assembly
objects.definition: An internal lining carried on timber battens or metal furring fixed in front of a masonry or concrete wall, creating a controlled support plane and a shallow service or levelling cavity.
functions: Provide a straight support plane over solid construction
Create space for services or insulation
Carry plasterboard, fibre-cement or decorative panels

cad.pattern: Parallel support runs fixed to a solid wall and overlaid by sheet or board modules
cad.placement: Internal face of masonry or concrete walls
cad.opening: Supports frame all required lining edges, openings and heavy attachment points
cad.load: Lining loads pass through supports and anchors into the solid wall

notes: Furring used here is an internal lining support; the existing cladding furring object remains a separate external-envelope role.

objects.name: multilayer internal lining assembly
objects.definition: A wall or ceiling lining with two or more superimposed sheet layers whose joints, fasteners and interfaces are coordinated as one documented build-up.
functions: Increase lining mass or robustness
Provide the layer build-up required by a selected fire or acoustic system
Keep joints and fixings coordinated between layers
not_synonyms: performance rating by layer count alone

cad.pattern: Coincident sheet fields with independent joint graphs and recorded layer order
cad.placement: On wall or ceiling supports where the selected system requires multiple layers
cad.start: Base lining layer at support plane
cad.opening: Layer returns and penetrations follow the selected documented system
cad.load: Combined layer self-weight transferred by the specified fastening sequence

notes: Layer count is geometry; FRL, sound rating and impact performance remain evidence and cannot be assumed from count alone.

objects.name: curved internal lining assembly
objects.definition: An internal wall or ceiling lining formed to a curve using flexible or suitably prepared sheets over closely set curved or faceted supports.
functions: Create a curved finished surface
Maintain continuous support and controlled sheet bending
Resolve curved joints, edges and openings
materials: flexible gypsum plasterboard or fibre-cement sheet
attributes: grain or machine direction where relevant

cad.pattern: Developable or faceted sheet surfaces following a controlled support curve
cad.placement: Curved feature walls, columns, soffits, arches and ceiling transitions
cad.opening: Openings require curved trimming and supported sheet edges
cad.load: Bent sheet reactions and self-weight transferred to repeated supports

notes: Allowable radius and forming method are selected-product data, not a universal value for all plasterboard or fibre cement.

objects.name: fibre-cement internal lining assembly
objects.definition: An internal wall or ceiling lining made from fibre-cement sheets or panels fixed to framing, furring or a documented masonry support system and finished with flush, expressed or covered joints.
functions: Provide a durable internal surface
Provide a lining substrate suitable for the selected exposure and finish
Form flush, expressed or prefinished panel layouts

cad.pattern: Sheet or panel modules tiled across supported internal planes
cad.placement: Internal walls and ceilings, including robust or moisture-prone locations where the selected product is suitable
cad.start: Supported sheet edge or perimeter trim
cad.end: Supported sheet edge, expressed joint or movement joint
cad.opening: All cut edges and openings use selected-system support and edge treatment
cad.load: Sheet self-weight and finish loads transferred through fasteners to supports

notes: A generic fibre-cement sheet is not automatically water-resistant construction; the complete wet-area system remains in the waterproofing discipline.

objects.name: decorative internal panel-lining assembly
objects.definition: A non-structural internal wall or ceiling finish made from repeated decorative sheets or panels with visible grooves, expressed joints, cover trims or concealed panel connections.
functions: Provide a finished decorative surface
Protect selected wall or ceiling areas
Organise repeated panel modules and edge details

cad.pattern: Repeated panel modules set out from a datum with explicit joints and perimeter cuts
cad.placement: Full-height or partial-height internal walls and selected ceilings
cad.end: Final module, opening or perimeter trim
cad.opening: Panels are cut, framed or trimmed around openings and accessories
cad.load: Panel self-weight transferred by selected adhesive and mechanical fixings

notes: A decorative panel may cover an existing plasterboard lining rather than replace it; substrate and layer order must remain explicit.

objects.name: internal timber panelling assembly
objects.definition: An internal wall or ceiling lining formed from solid timber appearance boards or engineered timber panels fixed to framing, battens, furring or another supported substrate.
functions: Provide a finished timber surface
Accommodate board or panel movement through the selected profile and joints
Create horizontal, vertical, diagonal or modular lining patterns

cad.pattern: Repeated narrow boards or sheet panels arranged from a datum over a support grid
cad.placement: Internal walls and ceilings protected from weather and unsuitable damp exposure unless the selected product says otherwise
cad.start: Datum board, panel or perimeter trim
cad.end: Last board or panel, opening or movement allowance
cad.opening: Cuts and trims retain movement gaps and support at openings
cad.load: Self-weight transferred through nails, screws, clips or combined adhesive fixing to supports

notes: Interior plywood to AS/NZS 2270 is for fully protected interior use; structural, wet-area and fire properties require separate evidence.

objects.name: direct-fixed plasterboard ceiling assembly
objects.definition: A plasterboard ceiling whose sheets are mechanically fixed, with documented adhesive where permitted, directly to ceiling joists, truss bottom chords, battens or direct-fix furring supports.
functions: Form a level or sloping internal ceiling face
Transfer plasterboard self-weight to closely spaced structure or battens
Coordinate joints, perimeter edges, access and service openings

ncc_references.relationship: Finished ceiling lining and underside geometry contribute to measured room height; the numerical height requirement remains analysis rather than a lining object.

cad.pattern: Sheets tiled across repeated joists, chords or battens with supported edges and documented butt joints
cad.placement: Below floor, roof or ceiling support members
cad.start: Room perimeter or ceiling setout datum
cad.end: Opposite perimeter, bulkhead or control joint
cad.opening: Light, grille, access and service openings are cut and independently supported as required
cad.load: Ceiling self-weight passes through fasteners and approved adhesive to supports

notes: Ceiling collapse risk is one reason the sheet, adhesive, fasteners and support plane must be separate model objects rather than one surface.

objects.name: concealed suspended plasterboard ceiling assembly
objects.definition: A plasterboard ceiling carried by a concealed metal grid hung below the building structure using suspension rods, clips or brackets, primary rails and secondary furring channels.
functions: Create an independently levelled ceiling plane
Provide a services zone below structure
Carry continuously jointed plasterboard while hiding the suspension grid

cad.pattern: Suspension points support primary rails; clips support perpendicular furring channels; sheet modules cover the grid
cad.placement: Below roof, floor or dedicated structural supports
cad.opening: Openings require framing, support and service coordination independent of the cut sheet
cad.load: Ceiling and approved service loads pass through grid and hangers to verified structure

notes: Suspension, bracing, anchorage and service loads require a designed selected system; this generic assembly only preserves the physical anatomy.

objects.name: exposed-grid suspended ceiling assembly
objects.definition: A suspended ceiling made from visible interlocking main and cross tees supported by hangers and perimeter trim, with removable tiles or panels laid into the resulting grid modules.
functions: Form a modular ceiling plane
Support removable ceiling tiles or panels
Provide accessible space for services above the ceiling
materials: galvanised or coated steel tee sections

cad.pattern: Orthogonal main-tee and cross-tee grid containing repeated removable tile modules
cad.placement: Suspended below structure with a continuous perimeter trim
cad.start: Verified suspension anchors and perimeter datum
cad.end: Exposed grid and lay-in tile face
cad.opening: Services replace, cut or bridge grid modules and require independent support where specified
cad.load: Grid and tile loads pass through hangers to structure; services are not assumed carried by the grid

notes: The visible grid and removable infill tiles are separate objects; a service fitting in a tile module is not automatically supported by the tile.

objects.name: ceiling suspension support system
objects.definition: The hangers, anchors, brackets, rails, channels or tees and perimeter members that carry a suspended ceiling below the primary building structure.
functions: Transfer ceiling loads to structure
Set and maintain the ceiling plane
Provide repeated supports for lining sheets, tiles or panels

cad.pattern: Repeated vertical suspension elements feeding one or two orthogonal horizontal support grids
cad.placement: Between primary structure and suspended ceiling face
cad.end: Lining, tile or panel support plane
cad.opening: Grid is trimmed, bridged or independently framed around services and access openings
cad.load: Designed ceiling loads transferred to structure through anchors and hangers

notes: A ceiling suspension system must not be assumed to support ducts, pipes, cable trays or other services unless explicitly designed for them.

objects.name: internal lining perimeter-junction assembly
objects.definition: The physical gap, backing, seal, tape, compound, bead, cornice or cover trim used where an internal lining terminates against a floor, wall, ceiling, column or other construction.
functions: Finish and protect the lining edge
Accommodate selected movement or tolerance
Provide required air, sound, moisture or fire continuity when part of a documented system

cad.pattern: Continuous linear junction following the perimeter of each lining field
cad.placement: At lining boundaries and changes of substrate or plane
cad.opening: Runs around openings where the selected detail requires it
cad.load: Non-structural edge protection, seal or trim load transferred locally

notes: A decorative cornice can hide a gap but does not automatically provide air, acoustic, moisture or fire sealing.

objects.name: internal lining movement-control joint assembly
objects.definition: A deliberate break through the lining finish, formed with separated sheet edges and the selected bead, trim, backing or sealant so movement is not forced into an ordinary stopped joint.
functions: Accommodate differential movement
Divide large or geometrically interrupted lining fields
Carry required finish or performance continuity without rigidly bridging the break

cad.pattern: Continuous break through the lining field with independent edges each side
cad.placement: At documented intervals, substrate changes, building joints and selected stress-concentration locations
cad.opening: May continue around or terminate at openings only as documented
cad.load: Separates finish loads and movement rather than transferring structural action across the gap

notes: The joint location and spacing are design and product inputs; they are not embedded here as a universal rule.

objects.name: internal lining service-opening assembly
objects.definition: A cut opening through an internal lining together with the trimming, backing, support, edge finish and seal needed for a light, grille, outlet, pipe, access item or other service interface.
functions: Provide a controlled service penetration or recess
Support cut lining edges and adjacent service hardware
Maintain required surface and performance continuity around the opening
attributes: fire, acoustic, air and moisture evidence

cad.pattern: Discrete opening subtracted from lining layers and surrounded by explicit support and edge components
cad.placement: At coordinated service positions in wall and ceiling linings
cad.opening: This object is the lining opening and does not replace the service body or its clearances
cad.load: Cut lining edges and approved lightweight fittings supported by documented framing; heavy services independently supported

notes: Fire, acoustic, moisture and airtightness continuity require the corresponding selected system; a drawn trim alone is not proof.

objects.name: internal lining repair-patch assembly
objects.definition: A replacement piece of lining fitted into a prepared damaged area and supported by backing or framing, with its perimeter joint reinforced, filled and finished to match the surrounding surface.
functions: Replace a local damaged lining area
Restore a continuous supported surface
Provide a finishable perimeter connection to sound existing lining
attributes: required fire, acoustic or moisture system repair evidence

cad.pattern: Discrete replacement panel within an existing lining field
cad.placement: At a prepared damaged or altered portion of wall or ceiling lining
cad.end: Finished patch surface blended into surrounding lining
cad.opening: Temporary repair opening is closed by the patch but retained in history
cad.load: Patch self-weight transferred through backing and fixings to sound surrounding construction

notes: Matching the visible surface does not automatically restore a tested fire, acoustic, impact or wet-area system; the repair method needs relevant evidence.

objects.name: standard gypsum plasterboard sheet
objects.definition: A factory-made paper-faced gypsum-core sheet intended for ordinary internal wall or ceiling lining where no special moisture, fire, acoustic, impact or exterior exposure grade has been selected.
functions: Form a smooth lining plane
Accept stopped joints and decorative finishes
Provide a modular sheet layer over supported framing or furring

cad.pattern: Rectangular sheets repeated over support members with explicit sheet edges
cad.placement: Ordinary dry internal wall and documented ceiling applications
cad.end: Supported, recessed or butt sheet edge
cad.opening: Cut around openings with required edge support
cad.load: Self-weight and finish load passed through fasteners and approved adhesive to supports

notes: Special-grade boards are separate objects or cross-discipline objects; colour is not a reliable grade identifier in the model.

objects.name: ceiling-grade plasterboard sheet
objects.definition: A gypsum plasterboard product selected for ceiling use, with its permitted support spacing and sag resistance taken from the chosen manufacturer and installation system.
functions: Form a horizontal or sloping ceiling face
Span between documented ceiling supports
Receive jointing and decoration

cad.pattern: Rectangular ceiling sheets crossing repeated supports
cad.placement: Below joists, battens, furring channels or a documented suspended grid
cad.end: Opposite perimeter, joint or control joint
cad.opening: Cut openings require selected support and trim
cad.load: Ceiling sheet self-weight transferred to every documented fixing line

notes: The selected product and exposure conditions determine ceiling suitability; the ontology does not infer it from thickness alone.

objects.name: high-density plasterboard sheet
objects.definition: A gypsum plasterboard sheet manufactured with greater core density or reinforced construction for a selected impact, fixing, sound or multi-performance application.
functions: Provide a more robust lining face
Carry documented light-duty attachments
Contribute selected impact or acoustic performance within a tested system

cad.pattern: Robust sheet modules fixed over a wall support grid
cad.placement: High-use internal wall areas or selected performance systems
cad.end: Supported sheet edge or movement joint
cad.opening: Opening edges retain required support and reinforcement
cad.load: Self-weight and only documented attachment loads transferred to supports

notes: High density, impact resistance and enhanced fixing capacity overlap in products but are stored as evidence, not treated as automatic synonyms.

objects.name: flexible plasterboard sheet
objects.definition: A thin or specially manufactured gypsum plasterboard sheet intended to bend to a documented radius when fixed over suitably close curved supports.
functions: Form curved lining surfaces
Reduce faceting compared with ordinary rigid sheet
Provide a finishable gypsum lining layer on curved framing
attributes: wet or dry forming method if permitted

cad.pattern: Developable sheet bent continuously across repeated curved supports
cad.placement: Curved walls, columns, arches, soffits and ceiling transitions
cad.opening: Curved openings require separate trimming and edge support
cad.load: Bent sheet reactions and self-weight transferred through dense fixing lines

notes: Minimum radius and forming method are selected-product limits and must not be generalised from another board.

objects.name: perforated acoustic plasterboard sheet
objects.definition: A gypsum plasterboard sheet manufactured with an open perforation pattern and usually an acoustic backing layer so a wall or ceiling surface can absorb sound within a documented system.
functions: Provide a perforated finished lining face
Admit sound energy to an absorptive backing or cavity
Create repeatable acoustic panel patterns

cad.pattern: Sheet modules containing a repeated perforation field and solid edge zones
cad.placement: Selected internal walls and concealed-grid ceilings
cad.opening: Service cuts interrupt the perforation field and need coordinated trims
cad.load: Sheet self-weight transferred to supports; acoustic backing retained independently

notes: Sound absorption and sound insulation are different properties; perforations do not by themselves create a separating-wall rating.

objects.name: fibre-reinforced gypsum lining sheet
objects.definition: A rigid gypsum-based lining sheet reinforced through its core or surfaces with fibres rather than relying only on conventional paper facings.
functions: Provide a robust gypsum lining or sheathing layer
Receive documented joints and finishes
Contribute selected impact, fire, moisture or fixing performance

cad.pattern: Rigid sheet modules over framing or furring
cad.placement: Selected internal lining systems only where supported by product documentation
cad.end: Supported sheet edge or documented joint
cad.opening: Cut edges follow the product joint and support system
cad.load: Self-weight and documented attachment loads transferred to supports

notes: Australian product terminology and applicable product standards vary; retain the selected product identity rather than mapping every gypsum-fibre board to AS/NZS 2588.

objects.name: general internal fibre-cement lining sheet
objects.definition: A flat cellulose-cement sheet selected as an internal lining for robust or moisture-prone walls or ceilings, with its particular exposure and finish limits taken from product documentation.
functions: Form a durable internal lining surface
Provide a substrate for paint, tiles or another documented finish
Resist ordinary knocks and selected moisture exposure

cad.pattern: Rectangular sheets with recessed or square edges over repeated supports
cad.placement: Internal walls and documented ceiling locations
cad.end: Supported edge, expressed joint or control joint
cad.opening: Cut edges require documented support, sealing or trim
cad.load: Sheet and applied finish loads transferred through specified fasteners

notes: This general object does not replace the dedicated wet-area substrate object or establish a waterproof system.

objects.name: decorative grooved fibre-cement lining sheet
objects.definition: An internal fibre-cement sheet with factory-routed or moulded face grooves that create a repeated board-like or geometric appearance after fixing and finishing.
functions: Provide a durable decorative lining face
Create repeated groove patterns without separate narrow boards
Accept selected coatings or prefinished surfaces
materials: factory-applied primer or finish where selected

cad.pattern: Rectangular sheet modules with parametric face grooves aligned across joints
cad.placement: Feature walls and documented ceiling applications
cad.end: Perimeter, opening or final aligned groove
cad.opening: Cuts must account for pattern and edge support
cad.load: Sheet self-weight transferred through specified fixings to supports

notes: Groove layout is visible geometry and should not be replaced with a texture when accurate cut lists or junctions are required.

objects.name: prefinished internal fibre-cement panel
objects.definition: A fibre-cement panel supplied with a factory-applied visible face and installed with an expressed, sealed or proprietary concealed joint system rather than site-stopped plasterboard-style joints.
functions: Provide a finished robust wall or ceiling face
Reduce site-applied surface finishing
Create a deliberate panel and joint layout

cad.pattern: Finished panel modules separated by explicit joint gaps or trims
cad.placement: Selected internal feature or high-use surfaces
cad.opening: Cuts and exposed edges use product-specific finish details
cad.load: Panel self-weight transferred through mechanical or documented combined fixing system

notes: The visible finish is integral to the selected panel record; replacement colour, batch and joint compatibility remain product data.

objects.name: interior plywood lining sheet
objects.definition: A non-structural plywood sheet selected for fully protected internal wall or ceiling panelling, usually with a visible veneer face and exposed, covered or shadow-gap joints.
functions: Provide a timber-faced internal lining
Create large modular wall or ceiling panels
Accept clear, stained or opaque finishes

cad.pattern: Large rectangular panels with visible grain direction and explicit joints
cad.placement: Fully protected internal walls and ceilings
cad.opening: Cut edges and grain pattern are coordinated with trims and support
cad.load: Panel self-weight transferred through nails, screws, clips or documented adhesive fixing

notes: Interior plywood is not assumed structural, wet-area suitable or exterior durable; those roles require other product evidence.

objects.name: interior blockboard lining panel
objects.definition: A fully protected interior panel made with a core of edge-laid timber strips faced with veneers, selected for non-structural wall or ceiling panelling or trim work.
functions: Provide a stiff timber-based panel lining
Create large finished interior modules
Accept veneer, paint or clear finishing

cad.pattern: Large rectangular panels with recorded core and face directions
cad.placement: Fully protected interior wall or ceiling locations
cad.opening: Cut edges receive documented trim or sealing
cad.load: Panel self-weight transferred to framing or battens through selected fixings

notes: Blockboard and plywood share AS/NZS 2270 scope but have different core geometry and should not be merged.

objects.name: MDF decorative lining panel
objects.definition: A medium-density fibreboard sheet or factory-profiled panel used as a non-structural decorative internal wall or ceiling lining in the exposure conditions permitted by the selected product.
functions: Provide a smooth or routed decorative surface
Create repeated grooves or moulded profiles
Accept paint, veneer or another selected face finish

cad.pattern: Full-height or dado-height panels with repeated machined face profiles
cad.placement: Protected internal walls and documented ceiling applications
cad.start: Floor gap, datum or lower trim
cad.end: Top gap, trim or ceiling junction
cad.opening: Cuts maintain expansion gaps and supported joints
cad.load: Panel self-weight transferred by movement-compatible adhesive plus specified mechanical fixings

notes: MR MDF means moisture resistant, not waterproof; wet-area use requires the exact product and system instructions.

objects.name: particleboard decorative lining panel
objects.definition: A resin-bonded wood-particle sheet used as a protected internal decorative panel or as a substrate for veneer, laminate or another factory-applied face.
functions: Provide a uniform panel substrate
Carry decorative veneer or laminate
Form repeated non-structural interior lining modules
materials: surface veneer or laminate where selected

cad.pattern: Rectangular decorative panels fixed to a support framework
cad.placement: Dry protected internal wall or ceiling locations permitted by the product
cad.opening: Exposed cut edges require appropriate sealing or trim
cad.load: Panel self-weight transferred through documented fixings to supports

notes: A veneered or laminated face does not change the particleboard core identity; flooring-grade particleboard is outside this object.

objects.name: hardboard internal lining sheet
objects.definition: A thin high-density wood-fibre sheet used in protected internal panelling, often with one smooth face and a textured back, and fixed over continuous or closely spaced support.
functions: Provide a thin smooth lining or backing surface
Form curved or flat decorative panels where documented
Accept paint or another selected finish

cad.pattern: Thin sheet modules over a backing frame or existing lining
cad.placement: Dry protected interior wall or ceiling panels
cad.opening: Thin cut edges require support and finish treatment
cad.load: Sheet self-weight transferred through close fixings or documented adhesive system

notes: Masonite is a proprietary term and is not used as the canonical name for every hardboard product.

objects.name: solid timber lining board
objects.definition: A narrow solid-timber appearance board installed in repeated courses as an internal wall or ceiling lining, with its profile and joints chosen to accommodate appearance and seasonal movement.
functions: Provide a natural timber finish
Cover framing, battens or another substrate
Distribute movement across repeated board joints

cad.pattern: Parallel repeated boards joined edge to edge over framing or battens
cad.placement: Protected internal walls and ceilings
cad.start: Datum board at corner, floor or ceiling
cad.end: Final trimmed board or perimeter gap
cad.opening: Boards are cut and trimmed around openings while retaining supported ends
cad.load: Board self-weight transferred through face, secret or clip fixings to supports

notes: Profile subclasses identify physical joint geometry; species and finish remain attributes.

objects.name: tongue-and-groove timber lining board
objects.definition: A solid timber lining board with a projecting tongue along one edge and matching groove along the other, commonly detailed with a small face V or shadow feature at each course.
functions: Interlock adjacent lining boards
Maintain face alignment
Mask small movement through the selected face profile

cad.pattern: Interlocking parallel boards with repeated tongue, groove and optional V-joint geometry
cad.placement: Internal wall or ceiling support grid
cad.end: Final tongue, groove or trimmed edge
cad.opening: Profiles terminate at supported trims around openings
cad.load: Each board individually fixed; interlock aligns but is not assumed to carry structural load

notes: A V-joint is a possible exposed face detail, not a synonym for every tongue-and-groove profile.

objects.name: shiplap timber lining board
objects.definition: A solid timber lining board with opposing rebated edges that overlap adjacent boards while allowing the selected visible gap and seasonal movement.
functions: Overlap adjacent lining courses
Accommodate movement without a tight tongue-and-groove joint
Create a repeated shadow or expressed line

cad.pattern: Parallel overlapping boards with repeated opposing rebates
cad.placement: Protected internal walls and ceilings
cad.opening: Board ends are supported and trimmed around openings
cad.load: Each board fixed to supports; overlap is not assumed structural

notes: Internal shiplap and external weather-exposed shiplap may look similar but have different product, moisture and envelope requirements.

objects.name: internal timber slat lining member
objects.definition: A narrow timber or timber-look member repeated with visible gaps over a backing surface or acoustic absorber to form a slatted internal wall or ceiling finish.
functions: Create a repeated linear decorative surface
Partially screen a backing layer
Contribute to a documented acoustic absorber when used with open gaps and backing

cad.pattern: Parallel repeated slats at a controlled centre spacing over a visible backing plane
cad.placement: Feature walls, ceilings and acoustic lining areas
cad.opening: Slats stop, trim or frame around openings
cad.load: Each slat transferred through clips or fixings to a carrier or substrate

notes: The term batten is common visually, but this object is a finish member and not a structural or lining-support batten.

objects.name: mineral-fibre lay-in ceiling tile
objects.definition: A lightweight mineral-fibre panel sized to rest on an exposed suspended tee grid and remain removable for access above the ceiling.
functions: Infill a modular exposed ceiling grid
Provide a finished ceiling face
Provide selected sound absorption, humidity or fire-hazard properties when documented

cad.pattern: Removable panels repeated one per exposed grid module
cad.placement: On main and cross tees in an exposed-grid ceiling
cad.opening: Services may replace or cut a tile but require documented support
cad.load: Tile self-weight bears on tee flanges; service loads excluded unless designed

notes: Acoustic ceiling tile is a functional description spanning several materials, so mineral fibre remains explicit.

objects.name: plasterboard lay-in ceiling tile
objects.definition: A small factory-cut or faced gypsum plasterboard panel made to sit within an exposed tee-grid ceiling module and remain individually removable.
functions: Infill an exposed ceiling grid
Provide a gypsum-faced modular ceiling
Allow tile-by-tile access above the ceiling

cad.pattern: Removable gypsum panels repeated in exposed grid modules
cad.placement: Exposed tee-grid suspended ceilings
cad.opening: Cut-outs require edge care and independent service support
cad.load: Tile self-weight bears on grid flanges

notes: A lay-in plasterboard tile is discrete and removable; it is not modelled as part of a continuously stopped ceiling sheet field.

objects.name: metal lay-in ceiling panel
objects.definition: A folded, pressed or clipped metal panel installed as a removable or demountable infill within a suspended ceiling grid or carrier system.
functions: Provide a durable modular ceiling face
Permit demountable access
Carry perforations and acoustic backing where selected
materials: acoustic tissue or pad where selected

cad.pattern: Repeated folded metal pans fitted to grid modules or carriers
cad.placement: Suspended ceiling grid or selected carrier system
cad.opening: Services use factory or site-cut apertures with independent support as required
cad.load: Panel self-weight and retention loads transferred to grid or carrier

notes: Perforated metal plus an absorber is an acoustic assembly; the metal panel alone is not assigned an absorption value.

objects.name: internal wall-lining furring channel
objects.definition: A light-gauge formed-metal channel fixed vertically or horizontally in front of a wall to create a straight support plane for internal lining sheets or panels.
functions: Support lining sheets or panels
Correct or offset the lining plane
Create a shallow cavity for services or insulation

cad.pattern: Parallel channel runs at selected centres across a wall face
cad.placement: In front of masonry, concrete or another documented substrate
cad.opening: Channels frame and support lining edges around openings
cad.load: Lining loads transferred through channel and clips or anchors to host wall

notes: The existing cladding furring channel has an external-envelope role; similar section geometry does not make the objects interchangeable.

objects.name: wall-lining furring clip
objects.definition: A formed metal clip or bracket anchored to a solid wall and shaped to hold, space or level an internal wall furring channel.
functions: Connect furring channel to the host wall
Set the channel offset and plane
Transfer lining loads into wall anchors

cad.pattern: Discrete clips repeated along each furring channel
cad.placement: Between solid wall and wall-lining furring channel
cad.opening: Additional clips may frame opening edges according to the selected system
cad.load: Channel and lining reactions transferred to the wall anchor

notes: Clip adjustment is physical; allowable stand-off and capacity are selected-product design data.

objects.name: internal lining timber batten
objects.definition: A straight timber member fixed to framing or a solid substrate to support internal lining boards or panels and establish their fixing plane.
functions: Provide a nailable or screw-fix support
Level or offset the lining plane
Support board ends, sheet joints and panel edges

cad.pattern: Parallel support members with additional perimeter and joint battens
cad.placement: On framing, masonry or concrete behind internal panels and boards
cad.opening: Battens frame sheet and board ends around openings
cad.load: Lining loads pass through batten fixings into substrate

notes: A decorative slat may share the same timber section but has a visible finish role; this batten remains concealed support.

objects.name: internal lining support packer
objects.definition: A thin discrete strip, plate or shim placed behind a batten, furring member, sheet edge or panel support to correct local alignment without becoming a continuous lining layer.
functions: Bring supports into a common plane
Fill a controlled local gap
Prevent unsupported rocking at a fixing point

cad.pattern: Discrete shims only where survey identifies a plane correction
cad.placement: Between substrate and batten, furring clip, channel or panel support
cad.opening: Not normally associated with openings except local frame alignment
cad.load: Compression and fixing reactions transferred between support and host

notes: Packing thickness should be modelled when it affects room dimensions, junctions or fixing embedment.

objects.name: concealed ceiling top cross rail
objects.definition: A primary horizontal light-gauge steel rail suspended below structure and used to carry perpendicular secondary ceiling furring channels through purpose-made clips.
functions: Form the primary suspended ceiling grid
Collect loads from secondary furring channels
Transfer grid loads to suspension rods, wires or brackets

cad.pattern: Parallel primary rails at designed centres below structure
cad.placement: Above concealed furring channels in a suspended ceiling
cad.end: Perimeter termination or joined rail end
cad.opening: Rails are trimmed or bridged around major openings according to design
cad.load: Secondary channel reactions transferred to suspension points

notes: Top Cross Rail is widely used Australian system terminology; TCR is retained as an abbreviation, not a brand-specific canonical name.

objects.name: concealed ceiling furring channel
objects.definition: A secondary light-gauge steel channel clipped below primary rails or direct-fix clips and providing the continuous face to which plasterboard ceiling sheets are screwed.
functions: Support plasterboard fixing lines
Set the finished ceiling plane
Distribute sheet loads to primary rails or direct-fix clips

cad.pattern: Parallel secondary channels crossing primary rails and aligning with lining fixing lines
cad.placement: Immediately above concealed plasterboard ceiling sheets
cad.end: Perimeter support or joined channel end
cad.opening: Extra channels frame sheet and service opening edges as designed
cad.load: Sheet loads transferred through clips to primary rails or direct-fix supports

notes: A furring channel can be suspended or direct fixed; support method is stored separately from the section identity.

objects.name: top cross rail joiner
objects.definition: A formed steel sleeve, splice or clip that aligns and connects the ends of two compatible primary top cross rails while permitting the selected system's continuity or movement detail.
functions: Splice primary ceiling rails
Maintain rail alignment
Transfer documented rail forces across the joint

cad.pattern: One connector at each documented primary-rail splice
cad.placement: Collinear ends of top cross rails
cad.opening: Rail joints are kept clear of incompatible opening details
cad.load: Documented rail forces transferred or released according to joiner type

notes: A splice joiner and a movement joint can look similar in plan but have different force-transfer roles.

objects.name: ceiling furring channel joiner
objects.definition: A purpose-made sleeve or clip joining collinear ceiling furring-channel lengths while keeping their plasterboard fixing faces aligned.
functions: Extend a furring-channel run
Align channel fixing faces
Transfer documented channel forces at the splice

cad.pattern: One joiner at each documented collinear furring-channel splice
cad.placement: Inside or around aligned channel ends
cad.opening: Splices are coordinated away from incompatible cut-outs and movement joints
cad.load: Channel reactions transferred according to selected joiner capacity

objects.name: ceiling cross-rail-to-furring-channel clip
objects.definition: A formed metal clip that locks a secondary ceiling furring channel below and perpendicular to a primary top cross rail.
functions: Connect primary and secondary ceiling grids
Hold the channel fixing face at the designed level
Transfer sheet and channel loads into the primary rail

cad.pattern: One clip at each primary-rail and furring-channel crossing
cad.placement: Orthogonal grid intersections
cad.opening: Additional or relocated intersections follow the designed opening frame
cad.load: Secondary grid reaction transferred to primary rail

notes: Interchange clip is system vocabulary and does not mean any generic crossing clip is interchangeable.

objects.name: ceiling suspension rod
objects.definition: A vertical steel rod, plain or threaded according to the selected system, that hangs a ceiling rail or grid bracket from a structural anchor above.
functions: Suspend the ceiling support grid
Set the ceiling drop
Transfer vertical ceiling loads to structure

cad.pattern: Vertical hanger points repeated on the designed suspension grid
cad.placement: Between structural anchor and ceiling rail or grid connector
cad.opening: Hangers are relocated or supplemented around openings by design
cad.load: Axial tension transfers ceiling load to structure

notes: A rod can be threaded, plain or system-specific; connection hardware must match rather than being inferred from diameter.

objects.name: ceiling suspension wire
objects.definition: A steel wire hanger looped, twisted or connected with approved fittings to suspend a ceiling grid member from a structural anchor.
functions: Suspend a ceiling grid
Provide an adjustable drop during installation
Transfer vertical ceiling loads through a tension-only element

cad.pattern: Repeated tension-only hanger lines above main grid members
cad.placement: Between structure and suspended ceiling grid
cad.opening: Hanger layout changes around openings only by documented design
cad.load: Axial tension transfers ceiling load to structure

notes: Suspension wire and seismic or lateral brace wire can use similar material but have different directions and force roles.

objects.name: ceiling suspension clip
objects.definition: A purpose-made metal connector joining a suspension rod or wire to a ceiling top cross rail, main tee or compatible support bracket.
functions: Connect hanger to ceiling grid
Permit documented height adjustment
Transfer hanger tension into the grid member

cad.pattern: One connector at each hanger-to-grid point
cad.placement: Bottom of suspension rod or wire
cad.opening: Additional clips accompany designed supplemental hangers around openings
cad.load: Grid reaction transferred to hanger

notes: The selected clip need only connect to the hanger type actually present; relationships list possible system families, not simultaneous use.

objects.name: ceiling suspension bracket
objects.definition: A formed metal bracket at the top or bottom of a ceiling hanger that connects the suspension element to structure or to a primary ceiling rail while providing selected adjustment.
functions: Provide a shaped hanger connection
Hold the suspension element at the required position
Transfer ceiling reactions between anchor, hanger and grid

cad.pattern: Discrete bracket at each selected suspension connection
cad.placement: Between anchor and hanger or hanger and primary rail
cad.opening: Supplemental brackets follow designed opening framing
cad.load: Connection shear and tension transferred through bracket fasteners

notes: Bracket and clip boundaries depend on product form; preserve manufacturer part identity when detailed fabrication is required.

objects.name: ceiling structural suspension anchor
objects.definition: A verified mechanical, cast-in, screwed or otherwise approved anchor connecting a suspended-ceiling hanger or bracket to the load-bearing structure above.
functions: Fix the ceiling suspension point to structure
Transfer hanger tension and designed lateral actions
Define the structural endpoint of the ceiling system

cad.pattern: Discrete anchors at each ceiling suspension or restraint point
cad.placement: Verified concrete, steel, timber or other load-bearing structure
cad.opening: Anchors avoid unverified slab zones, services and edges according to design
cad.load: Ceiling tension and designed lateral actions transferred into primary structure

notes: A fastener into plasterboard, insulation or non-structural lining is not a structural suspension anchor.

objects.name: concealed ceiling perimeter wall track
objects.definition: A light-gauge metal track or angle fixed around walls to locate, support or finish the ends of concealed ceiling furring channels and plasterboard edges.
functions: Establish the ceiling perimeter datum
Support or retain channel and sheet edges as designed
Provide a straight ceiling-to-wall termination

cad.pattern: Continuous track around the ceiling perimeter with mitred or butted corners
cad.placement: At concealed suspended ceiling-to-wall junction
cad.opening: Interrupted or framed around high-level openings as documented
cad.load: Perimeter sheet or channel reactions transferred through wall fixings where the design assigns support

notes: Some details use the perimeter only for location, others for support; this role must be a selected-system attribute.

objects.name: direct-fix ceiling channel clip
objects.definition: A short formed metal clip fixed directly to joists, trusses or another verified support to hold a ceiling furring channel at a small adjustable offset without a primary suspended rail.
functions: Connect furring channel directly to structure
Level a shallow ceiling cavity
Transfer channel and lining loads to supports

cad.pattern: Discrete clips repeated along each furring-channel run at support crossings
cad.placement: Between roof, floor or ceiling structure and furring channel
cad.opening: Supplementary clips accompany designed opening framing
cad.load: Furring and lining loads transferred directly into structure

notes: Direct fix describes the channel support method, not adhesive fixing of the plasterboard sheet.

objects.name: exposed ceiling-grid main tee
objects.definition: The primary visible inverted-T section in an exposed suspended ceiling grid, supported by hangers and fitted with connection points for cross tees.
functions: Form the primary grid lines
Support tile edges and cross tees
Transfer grid and tile loads to suspension hangers

cad.pattern: Parallel primary tee runs at the selected ceiling module
cad.placement: Suspended below structure and above tile plane
cad.opening: Main tees are trimmed and independently supported around major openings as designed
cad.load: Tile, cross-tee and grid loads transferred to hanger points

notes: The exposed flange is both support and finish geometry and should remain visible in the model.

objects.name: exposed ceiling-grid cross tee
objects.definition: A secondary visible inverted-T section that locks between main tees to divide an exposed ceiling grid into tile-sized modules.
functions: Divide the main grid into modules
Support transverse tile edges
Transfer tile loads to main tees

cad.pattern: Repeated secondary tees between main tees at tile-module intervals
cad.placement: Perpendicular to exposed-grid main tees
cad.opening: Cross tees are removed, shortened or supplemented around service modules by design
cad.load: Tile-edge loads transferred to main tees

notes: Cross-tee end connectors are normally integral product geometry, not assumed universal loose clips.

objects.name: exposed ceiling-grid perimeter angle
objects.definition: A visible or shadowed wall angle, channel or trim fixed around the room perimeter to locate and support the cut ends of an exposed tee grid and edge tiles as designed.
functions: Establish the exposed-grid ceiling level
Support or retain perimeter grid and tile edges
Finish the ceiling-to-wall junction

cad.pattern: Continuous perimeter member following walls and columns
cad.placement: At exposed-grid ceiling level around room boundaries
cad.opening: Continues around columns and bulkheads where detailed
cad.load: Perimeter tile and grid reactions transferred through wall fixings where assigned

notes: The profile may be a simple angle, channel or shadow trim; selected-system geometry controls the object subtype.

objects.name: ceiling-tile hold-down clip
objects.definition: A small spring or formed clip that retains a lay-in ceiling tile or panel against the exposed grid so it cannot lift or rattle under the documented conditions.
functions: Restrain tile uplift
Reduce tile movement or rattle
Keep selected panels seated on grid flanges

cad.pattern: Discrete clips at selected tile-to-grid edges
cad.placement: Above tee flange and against tile edge or back
cad.opening: Service tiles retain clips only where compatible with access and maintenance
cad.load: Tile uplift reaction transferred into grid

notes: Hold-down clips may be required only in selected locations or conditions; do not populate every tile by default.

objects.name: lining sheet-edge backing member
objects.definition: A timber or metal member placed behind a lining edge, butt joint, corner, patch or opening to provide a continuous fixing surface where the main framing does not coincide with the edge.
functions: Support lining edges
Provide fixing purchase
Keep adjacent sheet faces aligned

cad.pattern: Local members following unsupported sheet edges and opening perimeters
cad.placement: Behind lining joints, patches, corners and cut-outs
cad.opening: Forms part of the opening or patch perimeter
cad.load: Local lining and fixing loads transferred to main framing or sound surrounding lining

notes: Backing for a plasterboard butt joint can also be a plasterboard strip; that distinct back-blocking object is recorded with joint materials.

objects.name: lining service-opening trimmer frame
objects.definition: A rectangular or shaped local frame of timber or metal members surrounding a lining cut-out to support sheet edges and the associated access panel, grille, light or other service interface.
functions: Define a stable rough opening
Support cut lining edges
Provide fixing points for service frames or trims without relying on unsupported sheet

cad.pattern: Closed or partly open frame following a coordinated service rough opening
cad.placement: Within wall or ceiling support grid around a lining cut-out
cad.opening: Defines the physical rough opening
cad.load: Lining edge and approved fitting loads transferred to surrounding support grid

notes: Heavy equipment and services require independent structural support; this frame is not assumed adequate because it surrounds the cut-out.

objects.name: plasterboard lining screw
objects.definition: A purpose-made screw with a head shaped to seat below the plasterboard face without tearing the liner, selected to fasten gypsum lining to timber or metal supports.
functions: Mechanically fix plasterboard to supports
Clamp the sheet without damaging its face liner
Transfer sheet loads into timber or steel framing

cad.pattern: Discrete fasteners repeated along every documented support line
cad.placement: Through plasterboard into timber or light-gauge steel supports
cad.opening: Supplementary fixing lines follow framed opening edges
cad.load: Sheet shear and pull-off transferred into support

notes: A generic plasterboard screw is not substituted into a tested fire system unless the selected system permits it.

objects.name: plasterboard lining nail
objects.definition: A purpose-made nail with a head and shank intended to fix plasterboard to timber framing without cutting through the paper face.
functions: Mechanically fix plasterboard to timber supports
Resist sheet withdrawal
Provide repeated edge and field attachment points

cad.pattern: Discrete nails repeated along documented timber support lines
cad.placement: Through plasterboard into timber framing or battens
cad.opening: Fixings follow supported opening edges
cad.load: Sheet pull-off and shear transferred into timber support

notes: Whether nails are permitted on a ceiling or performance system is a selected-system rule, not inferred from the fastener name.

objects.name: gypsum-lining stud adhesive
objects.definition: A purpose-made adhesive applied in discrete daubs or beads between gypsum plasterboard and timber or metal framing as part of an approved combined adhesive-and-mechanical fixing system.
functions: Bond plasterboard to framing
Distribute sheet support between mechanical fixings
Reduce local movement and fastener demand where the system permits

cad.pattern: Discrete adhesive daubs or controlled beads along support faces between excluded fastener zones
cad.placement: Between plasterboard back and compatible timber or metal framing
cad.opening: Adhesive layout changes around openings and sheet edges according to the selected system
cad.load: Bond shear and peel shared with required mechanical fixings

notes: Adhesive is not a substitute for every required mechanical fixing, especially at perimeters, openings, ceilings or performance systems.

objects.name: masonry direct-fix lining adhesive bed
objects.definition: A discrete bed or ribbon of compatible adhesive placed between a prepared masonry or concrete surface and the back of a direct-fixed plasterboard lining.
functions: Bond plasterboard to a solid substrate
Bridge small permitted surface irregularities
Transfer lining weight into masonry or concrete
materials: gypsum-based or polymer-modified masonry lining adhesive

cad.pattern: Discrete adhesive beds arrayed behind each sheet according to the selected direct-fix system
cad.placement: Between solid wall and plasterboard back
cad.opening: Beds and edge support follow documented opening and perimeter details
cad.load: Sheet self-weight and local face actions transferred by cured bond to solid substrate

notes: The adhesive-bed pattern is product and substrate specific; dot and dab is retained only as a search term.

objects.name: plasterboard back-blocking adhesive
objects.definition: A compatible setting adhesive spread between the back of adjoining plasterboard sheets and a plasterboard backing strip to reinforce a butt joint or another documented joint zone.
functions: Bond the back-block to adjoining sheets
Spread joint movement over a wider zone
Keep unsupported butt-joint faces aligned

cad.pattern: Continuous adhesive beds behind both sides of a selected plasterboard joint
cad.placement: Between sheet backs and a back-blocking strip
cad.opening: Back-blocking is interrupted or specially detailed at openings
cad.load: Joint peel and bending reactions spread into adjoining sheet backs

notes: Some proprietary adhesives can serve more than one use, but the installed back-blocking bed remains a distinct physical role.

objects.name: plasterboard back-blocking strip
objects.definition: A strip cut from compatible plasterboard and bonded across the back of a sheet joint to reinforce, align and widen the effective joint zone.
functions: Bridge the back of a plasterboard joint
Support adjoining sheet edges
Distribute joint stress behind the face finish

cad.pattern: Continuous or segmented strips centred behind selected sheet joints
cad.placement: On the concealed back face of adjoining plasterboard sheets
cad.opening: Back-block path is coordinated with supports and openings
cad.load: Joint bending spread into a wider sheet zone through adhesive bond

notes: Back blocking is not wall nogging: it bonds to the lining sheets and may sit between structural supports.

objects.name: fibre-cement lining screw
objects.definition: A corrosion-appropriate screw with a head and thread selected to fix internal fibre-cement lining sheet to timber or light-gauge steel supports without unacceptable face damage.
functions: Mechanically fix fibre-cement sheet
Clamp the sheet to timber or steel supports
Transfer sheet and applied-finish loads into framing

cad.pattern: Discrete screws repeated along support lines and sheet edges
cad.placement: Through fibre-cement sheet into timber or steel supports
cad.start: Head at or below sheet face as detailed
cad.opening: Supplementary fixings follow framed opening edges
cad.load: Sheet pull-off, shear and finish loads transferred to support

notes: Fastener material and coating must suit the lining, support and exposure; a similar-looking drywall screw is not assumed compatible.

objects.name: fibre-cement lining nail
objects.definition: A corrosion-appropriate nail with a head, shank and length selected to fix internal fibre-cement lining sheet to timber framing or battens.
functions: Fix fibre-cement sheet to timber supports
Resist sheet withdrawal
Provide repeated face or concealed attachment points

cad.pattern: Discrete nails repeated along documented timber support lines
cad.placement: Through fibre-cement sheet into timber framing or battens
cad.opening: Fixings follow supported opening edges
cad.load: Sheet pull-off and shear transferred into timber support

notes: Selected product documentation controls whether nail fixing is permitted for the sheet, location and finish.

objects.name: decorative lining panel adhesive
objects.definition: A compatible construction or panel adhesive applied between a decorative timber, MDF, plywood, fibre-cement or other panel and its framing, batten or sheet substrate.
functions: Bond a decorative panel to its support
Distribute load between mechanical fixings
Reduce visible face fixings where the selected system permits

cad.pattern: Controlled beads or areas between panel back and support, clear of required movement gaps
cad.placement: Behind decorative panels on framing, battens or a suitable existing lining
cad.opening: Adhesive setout changes around cut-outs and unsupported panel edges
cad.load: Bond shares panel self-weight and face actions with required mechanical fixings

notes: Wood oils, panel coatings, moisture and movement affect compatibility; generic adhesive geometry does not prove a suitable bond.

objects.name: decorative lining panel nail
objects.definition: A visible, punched, filled or concealed nail selected to fix timber boards, MDF sheets, plywood or similar decorative internal lining panels to timber supports.
functions: Mechanically retain decorative panels
Provide immediate restraint while adhesive cures
Transfer panel loads to timber framing or battens

cad.pattern: Discrete nails at support crossings, board shoulders or panel edges
cad.placement: Through decorative board or panel into timber supports
cad.start: Visible face or concealed profile shoulder
cad.opening: Nail setout follows supported panel and board ends around openings
cad.load: Panel withdrawal and shear transferred into timber support

notes: Secret nailing describes placement at a board profile; it is not a separate nail material unless the selected product differs.

objects.name: decorative lining panel screw
objects.definition: A visible or concealed screw selected to fasten a removable or robust decorative lining panel to timber, metal framing, battens or a proprietary carrier.
functions: Mechanically retain a decorative panel
Permit documented removal or replacement
Transfer panel loads to supports

cad.pattern: Discrete screws repeated at panel support points
cad.placement: Through panel face, edge or concealed fixing zone into support
cad.start: Screw head at visible or concealed panel face
cad.opening: Fixings follow supported cuts and removable panel zones
cad.load: Panel shear and pull-off transferred into support

notes: A screw can make a panel demountable only when access to the head and the joint layout allow removal.

objects.name: concealed lining panel clip
objects.definition: A purpose-made clip fixed to a panel edge, groove, back or carrier so a decorative lining panel or board can be retained without visible face fasteners.
functions: Conceal panel attachment
Locate and retain panel edges
Permit movement or demounting where the selected clip system provides it

cad.pattern: Discrete clips repeated along panel edges, grooves or rear carriers
cad.placement: Between decorative panel and framing, batten or carrier
cad.end: Panel groove, edge or back engagement
cad.opening: Clip pattern adjusts around panel cuts and openings
cad.load: Panel reactions transferred through clip and its fixing to support

notes: Clip geometry is product-specific; secret fixing does not mean all panel clips interoperate.

objects.name: lining repair backing clip
objects.definition: A small metal or polymer clip inserted behind an existing lining edge to hold a repair patch or backing strip where conventional framing cannot be reached.
functions: Support a repair patch edge
Provide a local screw-fixing point
Avoid enlarging a repair opening solely to reach framing

cad.pattern: Discrete clips around a repair opening where solid backing is absent
cad.placement: Behind sound existing lining and patch edge
cad.opening: Located around the prepared repair opening
cad.load: Patch-edge load transferred into surrounding lining within product limits

notes: A repair clip is not assumed to restore a performance-rated assembly or support a heavy attachment.

objects.name: plasterboard recessed-edge joint assembly
objects.definition: A flush-finished joint between factory-recessed plasterboard edges, built from the recessed sheet shoulders, embedded paper tape, base compound and finishing compound.
functions: Connect adjacent recessed sheet edges
Reinforce the joint against cracking
Build the recess to a smooth finishable plane

cad.pattern: Continuous linear joint along paired factory-recessed sheet edges
cad.placement: Between plasterboard sheets within a wall or ceiling field
cad.opening: Joint terminates or is redirected at openings as detailed
cad.load: Non-structural surface continuity; local movement distributed by tape and compound

notes: A smooth visible result is not represented by one line: the tape and successive compound layers are retained as physical components.

objects.name: plasterboard butt-joint assembly
objects.definition: A flush-finished joint between square-cut or non-recessed plasterboard sheet ends, using backing or back-blocking where required and a wider taped compound finish over the flat sheet faces.
functions: Connect non-recessed sheet ends
Support and align the adjoining edges
Feather the raised joint over a wider surface zone

cad.pattern: Continuous joint across sheet ends, commonly staggered between adjacent courses
cad.placement: At non-recessed plasterboard sheet ends
cad.start: Sheet field edge or joint endpoint
cad.opening: Butt joints are coordinated away from stress-concentrating opening corners where required
cad.load: Joint movement distributed through backing, tape and broad compound finish

notes: Butt joint describes sheet-edge geometry, not poor workmanship; its finish normally differs from a recessed joint.

objects.name: plasterboard paper joint tape
objects.definition: A strong paper strip embedded in wet base compound to reinforce plasterboard sheet joints and internal corners before the finishing coats are applied.
functions: Bridge the plasterboard joint
Reinforce compound against cracking
Form a crisp fold at internal corners when creased

cad.pattern: Continuous narrow strip centred along each taped joint
cad.placement: Embedded within base compound over plasterboard joints and internal corners
cad.opening: Tape paths terminate, overlap or turn at opening corners according to the selected system
cad.load: Tension reinforcement across the compound joint

notes: System-specific fire and acoustic joint tapes remain separate objects because an ordinary paper tape cannot be presumed interchangeable.

objects.name: fibreglass mesh lining joint tape
objects.definition: An open glass-fibre mesh strip embedded in or bonded beneath a compatible jointing compound for selected plasterboard repair, fibre-cement or specialty lining joints.
functions: Reinforce a compatible joint compound
Bridge small gaps while compound keys through the mesh
Provide local crack control in selected systems

cad.pattern: Continuous mesh strip centred over selected joints or repairs
cad.placement: Within a compatible compound system
cad.opening: Mesh turns or terminates at opening corners as documented
cad.load: Distributed tensile reinforcement within compound

notes: Paper and mesh tapes are not default substitutes; the selected board and compound system controls their use.

objects.name: setting-type plasterboard base compound
objects.definition: A gypsum-based powder mixed with water and chemically set after application, used to embed tape and fill the deeper base layers of plasterboard joints.
functions: Embed joint tape
Fill recessed or butt-joint build-up
Harden by chemical setting before finishing coats

cad.pattern: Narrow-to-wide feathered layers following taped joint paths
cad.placement: Within plasterboard recesses, butt-joint build-up and corners
cad.opening: Compound follows taped returns and corners at openings
cad.load: Non-structural joint fill and tape embedment

notes: Setting time is a product property; a hardened base coat remains a thin physical finish layer in the model.

objects.name: drying-type plasterboard base compound
objects.definition: A premixed or ready-to-use plasterboard compound that hardens mainly by water loss and is selected for tape embedment or base coats where the system permits.
functions: Embed compatible joint tape
Fill joint recesses
Harden by drying before subsequent coats

cad.pattern: Feathered layers following selected plasterboard joint paths
cad.placement: Within joint recess and over tape where product instructions permit
cad.opening: Follows taped opening corners and returns
cad.load: Non-structural joint fill and tape embedment

notes: Drying and setting compounds harden differently; drying time depends strongly on coat thickness and ambient conditions.

objects.name: plasterboard finishing compound
objects.definition: A fine, readily sanded compound applied in the final feathered coat or coats over plasterboard joint base layers, fastener heads, beads and repairs.
functions: Create a smooth final joint surface
Feather transitions onto board faces
Cover fastener heads and bead flanges before decoration

cad.pattern: Wide thin feathered finish bands following joints, beads and fastener lines
cad.placement: Outermost joint compound layer before primer or decoration
cad.opening: Feathering continues around opening corners and trims
cad.load: Non-structural surface finishing layer

notes: The named level of finish is a workmanship and viewing-condition requirement, not a separate compound object.

objects.name: all-purpose plasterboard joint compound
objects.definition: A compound documented for more than one plasterboard jointing stage, such as tape embedment, base filling and finishing, within the limits of the selected product.
functions: Perform multiple compatible jointing coats
Embed tape where approved
Finish joints, beads and fastener heads

cad.pattern: One or more feathered layers following joint and bead paths
cad.placement: At stages explicitly permitted by the product
cad.opening: Compound follows detailed opening returns and corners
cad.load: Non-structural joint reinforcement embedment and finish

notes: All-purpose is a documented product capability, not permission to substitute it for every base or finish compound.

objects.name: plasterboard internal-corner tape joint
objects.definition: A concave internal corner between plasterboard faces finished by bedding creased paper tape into compound and feathering compound onto both wall or ceiling planes.
functions: Reinforce the internal corner
Cover the gap between intersecting sheets
Create a straight finishable arris

cad.pattern: Continuous concave line at intersecting plasterboard planes
cad.placement: Wall-to-wall and selected wall-to-ceiling internal corners
cad.opening: Turns and terminates at openings or junctions as detailed
cad.load: Surface reinforcement across the corner gap

notes: Where movement is expected, a flexible or separated junction may be required instead of rigid tape and compound.

objects.name: plasterboard external-corner bead
objects.definition: A rigid perforated or paper-faced metal or polymer section fixed over an external plasterboard corner and covered with compound to create a straight impact-resistant arris.
functions: Align and protect an external corner
Provide a compound key or paper bond
Create a straight finished arris

cad.pattern: Continuous rigid section along each exposed external plasterboard corner
cad.placement: External wall corners, nibs, reveals and bulkhead edges
cad.opening: Common around door and window reveals
cad.load: Local impact distributed into compound and lining faces

notes: Corner bead material and nose shape affect the visible arris and should be retained in detailed models.

objects.name: plasterboard internal-corner bead
objects.definition: A purpose-made metal, polymer or paper-faced section used in selected concave plasterboard corners to hold a straight angle and reinforce the joint before compound finishing.
functions: Align an internal corner
Reinforce the corner finish
Provide a controlled compound edge or flexible centre where designed

cad.pattern: Continuous section along selected internal plasterboard corners
cad.placement: Concave wall, ceiling, reveal or bulkhead junctions
cad.opening: Turns and terminates at opening junctions
cad.load: Local finish reinforcement only

notes: Internal corners are commonly paper taped; a bead is generated only when the selected detail specifies one.

objects.name: plasterboard stopping bead
objects.definition: A metal or polymer edge section fixed to a plasterboard termination so joint compound can stop cleanly at a straight exposed line.
functions: Protect a plasterboard cut edge
Provide a straight compound stop
Form a clean junction to another material, gap or opening

cad.pattern: Continuous edge section following a lining termination
cad.placement: At openings, material changes, exposed sheet ends and selected perimeters
cad.opening: Commonly follows door, window, access and service opening edges
cad.load: Edge protection and finish support only

notes: Stopping bead is the broad function; casing and shadowline profiles are distinct geometry subclasses.

objects.name: plasterboard casing bead
objects.definition: A stopping profile, often J-shaped or hooked, that encloses and protects the exposed thickness of a plasterboard edge at an opening or material junction.
functions: Cap the plasterboard edge
Create a straight reveal or abutment
Provide a compound stop or exposed finished return

cad.pattern: Continuous enclosing profile along exposed plasterboard edges
cad.placement: Door, window, access, service and material-transition edges
cad.opening: Directly forms the finished edge of an opening
cad.load: Edge protection and finish support only

notes: J bead is a common profile description but selected dimensions must match the board thickness and finish detail.

objects.name: plasterboard shadowline stopping bead
objects.definition: A shaped lining-edge profile that creates a deliberate narrow recessed shadow gap between plasterboard and an adjacent wall, ceiling, frame, column or material.
functions: Form a straight shadow gap
Terminate and protect the lining edge
Separate visually adjacent planes or materials

cad.pattern: Continuous recessed edge profile along a selected lining perimeter
cad.placement: Wall-to-ceiling, wall-to-frame, column and material-change junctions
cad.opening: Often follows opening reveals and frame perimeters
cad.load: Edge protection and finish support only

notes: A shadowline is visible geometry; it does not automatically accommodate building movement or provide an air, acoustic or fire seal.

objects.name: internal lining control-joint bead
objects.definition: A paired, flexible-centred or separable profile installed at a deliberate break in plasterboard or fibre-cement lining to form and protect the edges of a movement-control joint.
functions: Create a straight controlled lining break
Protect separated lining edges
Permit the documented small movement across or within the profile

cad.pattern: Continuous bead along each documented lining control-joint path
cad.placement: Between separately supported lining edges
cad.opening: Path around or into openings follows the selected detail
cad.load: Allows or localises finish movement rather than bridging structural load

notes: Movement range and fire, acoustic or air continuity are system properties and must be documented separately.

objects.name: fibre-cement flush-joint assembly
objects.definition: A site-finished joint between compatible recessed-edge fibre-cement sheets using the manufacturer's reinforcement tape and base and finishing compounds to create a nominally continuous surface.
functions: Join recessed fibre-cement sheet edges
Reinforce and fill the joint
Create a paintable or otherwise finishable flush surface

cad.pattern: Continuous reinforced finish band along compatible recessed sheet edges
cad.placement: Between flush-jointed internal fibre-cement sheets
cad.opening: Joints terminate and corners are reinforced according to the selected system
cad.load: Surface continuity and local crack distribution only

notes: Fibre-cement and plasterboard joint compounds are not assumed compatible even when both produce a flush visible surface.

objects.name: fibre-cement expressed-joint assembly
objects.definition: A deliberate visible gap or cover-trim joint between square-edge fibre-cement panels, with the selected backing, seal, trim or open-joint treatment and supported panel edges.
functions: Separate adjacent panel modules visibly
Accommodate selected tolerances and movement
Protect or seal panel edges as required by the documented system

cad.pattern: Continuous visible lines between panel modules
cad.placement: At square-edge fibre-cement or decorative panel boundaries
cad.opening: Joint grid aligns or terminates at opening edges as detailed
cad.load: Panel edges independently supported; joint trim carries only documented local actions

notes: Expressed describes the visible joint; whether it is open, sealed, backed or covered remains explicit.

objects.name: fibre-cement lining joint tape
objects.definition: An alkali-resistant reinforcing tape specified by the selected fibre-cement lining system and embedded in compatible base compound over flush joints and selected corners.
functions: Bridge fibre-cement sheet joints
Reinforce the cementitious or polymer joint compound
Distribute local movement across the joint finish
materials: alkali-resistant glass mesh or proprietary reinforcement

cad.pattern: Continuous reinforcement centred along compatible fibre-cement joints
cad.placement: Embedded within fibre-cement joint base coat
cad.opening: Tape turns or terminates at opening corners as documented
cad.load: Tension reinforcement within joint compound

notes: Tape selection belongs to the exact fibre-cement joint system; similar mesh appearance is not sufficient evidence.

objects.name: fibre-cement lining joint base coat
objects.definition: A compatible cementitious or polymer-modified compound used to fill recessed fibre-cement sheet joints and embed the specified reinforcing tape.
functions: Fill the fibre-cement joint recess
Embed joint reinforcement
Bond the joint build-up to compatible sheet edges

cad.placement: Between sheet edges and around embedded joint tape
cad.opening: Follows reinforced opening corners and returns

objects.name: fibre-cement lining joint top coat
objects.definition: A fine compatible finishing compound applied over a fibre-cement joint base coat and feathered onto the sheet face before the selected surface coating.
functions: Smooth the fibre-cement joint
Feather the joint onto adjacent sheet faces
Provide a compatible substrate for decoration

cad.pattern: Thin feathered bands along completed fibre-cement joints
cad.placement: Outermost joint finish before paint or another coating
cad.opening: Finish follows opening corners and edge beads as detailed
cad.load: Non-structural surface finishing layer

notes: Top coat here means the final joint compound, not the room's decorative paint topcoat.

objects.name: internal panel-joint cover strip

objects.name: internal cornice adhesive

Join cornice lengths and mitres where the product permits
